newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.K. cereals farmers face area aid cut on July 1.
newsitem.headline: U.K. cereals farmers face area aid cut on July 1.

text.p: British farmers stand to suffer a 2.89 percent cut in cereals and oilseeds area payments from July 1 as a result of a revaluation of the sterling green rate, British agriculture sources said on Thursday.
The British green rate was revalued on Thursday to 0.720829 per Ecu, from 0.742320, to close the gap caused by a further strengthening of sterling.

The sources said that as a result of the revaluation Britain would exceed the 11.5 percent compensation limit set by EU farm ministers on March 19 and that British farmers would therefore face a cut in 1997/98 (July/June) arable area payments.
But livestock aid rates, which were set on January 1, would apply until the end of 1997.
Green rates are used by the European Union to convert EU farm subsidies and institutional prices from Ecus into national currencies.
